name: Moses
charge: Refusing to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter; faithful in all the Lord's house; very meek, above all the men upon the face of the earth
summary: He gave up the court of Egypt to be counted with slaves, and led them forty years through a wilderness that murmured against him at every turn. The Lord's testimony on him is unmatched: my servant Moses, who is faithful in all mine house; with him will I speak mouth to mouth. He was buried by God.
offense: The record puts the first act at the point of choice rather than at the burning bush. Grown, and with the court of Egypt open to him, he refused to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter (Hebrews 11:24) and chose to be counted with slaves, esteeming reproach greater riches than the treasures of Egypt (Hebrews 11:26). What follows is forty years of a specific and unglamorous obedience: building the tabernacle to specification, so that as the Lord commanded Moses, so did he is repeated through the whole account of it, and enduring a congregation that murmured against him at every stage (Exodus 33:7). Numbers gives the character in one line that he did not write about himself, that he was very meek above all men on the face of the earth (Numbers 12:3). His own failure at Meribah is a separate case, and its inclusion here would be dishonest.
judgment: The commendation given to him is unlike any other in the Old Testament. Where a prophet receives visions and dreams, God says of Moses that he is faithful in all mine house (Numbers 12:7), and that he will speak with him mouth to mouth (Numbers 12:8), apparently, and not in dark speeches. He spoke as a man speaks to his friend. He asked to be blotted out of the book rather than see the nation destroyed and was not rebuked for asking. He was refused the land for the one failure and buried by God himself in a grave no man knows, and he stands on the mount with Elijah at the transfiguration, so that the man barred from the land is seen standing in it.

verses.text: By faith Moses, when he was come to years, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter;
Choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season;
Esteeming the reproach of Christ greater riches than the treasures in Egypt: for he had respect unto the recompence of the reward.
By faith he forsook Egypt, not fearing the wrath of the king: for he endured, as seeing him who is invisible.
(Now the man Moses was very meek, above all the men which were upon the face of the earth.)
And he said, Hear now my words: If there be a prophet among you, I the Lord will make myself known unto him in a vision, and will speak unto him in a dream.
My servant Moses is not so, who is faithful in all mine house.
With him will I speak mouth to mouth, even apparently, and not in dark speeches; and the similitude of the Lord shall he behold: wherefore then were ye not afraid to speak against my servant Moses?

And the Lord spake unto Moses face to face, as a man speaketh unto his friend. And he turned again into the camp: but his servant Joshua, the son of Nun, a young man, departed not out of the tabernacle.
And it came to pass on the morrow, that Moses said unto the people, Ye have sinned a great sin: and now I will go up unto the Lord; peradventure I shall make an atonement for your sin.
And Moses returned unto the Lord, and said, Oh, this people have sinned a great sin, and have made them gods of gold.
Yet now, if thou wilt forgive their sin—; and if not, blot me, I pray thee, out of thy book which thou hast written.
According to all that the Lord commanded Moses, so the children of Israel made all the work.
And Moses did look upon all the work, and, behold, they had done it as the Lord had commanded, even so had they done it: and Moses blessed them.
So Moses the servant of the Lord died there in the land of Moab, according to the word of the Lord.
And he buried him in a valley in the land of Moab, over against Beth–peor: but no man knoweth of his sepulchre unto this day.
And Moses was an hundred and twenty years old when he died: his eye was not dim, nor his natural force abated.
And the children of Israel wept for Moses in the plains of Moab thirty days: so the days of weeping and mourning for Moses were ended.
And Joshua the son of Nun was full of the spirit of wisdom; for Moses had laid his hands upon him: and the children of Israel hearkened unto him, and did as the Lord commanded Moses.
And there arose not a prophet since in Israel like unto Moses, whom the Lord knew face to face,
In all the signs and the wonders, which the Lord sent him to do in the land of Egypt to Pharaoh, and to all his servants, and to all his land,
And in all that mighty hand, and in all the great terror which Moses shewed in the sight of all Israel.
And he brought out of him a merciful man, which found favour in the sight of all flesh, even Moses, beloved of God and men, whose memorial is blessed.
He made him like to the glorious saints, and magnified him, so that his enemies stood in fear of him.
By his words he caused the wonders to cease, and he made him glorious in the sight of kings, and gave him a commandment for his people, and shewed him part of his glory.
He sanctified him in his faithfuless and meekness, and chose him out of all men.

He made him to hear his voice, and brought him into the dark cloud, and gave him commandments before his face, even the law of life and knowledge, that he might teach Jacob his covenants, and Israel his judgments.
And, behold, there appeared unto them Moses and Elias talking with him.

text.text: And, behold, there appeared unto them Moses and Elias talking with him.

entries.commentary: Miriam and Aaron spake against Moses because of the Ethiopian woman whom he had married. This is still Zipporah, the daughter of the priest of Midian, whom Moses married in the forty years he dwelt outside Egypt, and whom the Lord allowed him to marry; a place being called Midian and the woman called an Ethiopian is no contradiction. They did not speak against Moses when he was saving them out of Egypt, nor when he set Aaron over the men and Miriam over the women; the murmuring came from somewhere else and they took hold of it. They said, Hath the LORD indeed spoken only by Moses? hath he not spoken also by us? And the LORD heard it.

The man Moses was very meek, above all the men which were upon the face of the earth. The Lord suddenly called Moses, Aaron, and Miriam to the tabernacle, came down in the pillar of the cloud, and called Aaron and Miriam forth. He declared the difference: to a prophet He makes Himself known in a vision and speaks in a dream, but with His servant Moses, faithful in all His house, He speaks mouth to mouth, even apparently, and not in dark speeches. Wherefore then were ye not afraid to speak against my servant Moses?

The anger of the Lord was kindled, and the cloud departed from off the tabernacle, and Miriam became leprous, white as snow. Aaron pleaded, Lay not the sin upon us; and Moses cried unto the Lord, Heal her now, O God, I beseech thee. The Lord answered that if her father had but spit in her face, she should be ashamed seven days; so she was shut out from the camp seven days, and the people journeyed not till Miriam was brought in again. The spit is correction, a father putting his child in her place; had she been raised to respect the men of the Lord, this would not have befallen her. This is a charge to raise children in the fear of the Lord and to teach them to respect the elders and the men of the Lord. Parents who let their children speak evil to the men of the Lord provoke them to wrath and bring judgment on the household.

The Lord said, Depart, and go up hence, thou and the people which thou hast brought up out of the land of Egypt, unto the land which I sware unto Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob; and I will send an angel before thee, and I will drive out the Canaanite, the Amorite, the Hittite, the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite. That Angel is Christ. I will not go up in the midst of thee, for thou art a stiffnecked people, lest I consume thee in the way. From the questions: a land flowing with milk and honey is not a magical land of milk. It means a plenteous, fertile land of great landscape, valleys, grass, and fields, with cattle and goats grazing for the milk, and flowers and plants in abundance for the bees to make the honey; a land blessed as the days of heaven upon the earth.

When the people heard these evil tidings, they mourned, and no man did put on him his ornaments; the Lord said, Put off thy ornaments from thee, that I may know what to do unto thee, and the children of Israel stripped themselves of their ornaments by the mount Horeb, while the Lord weighed whether to come up into the midst of them in a moment and consume them.

Moses took the tabernacle and pitched it without the camp, afar off from the camp, and called it the Tabernacle of the congregation. The Lord dwelt there, and he would not sit in the midst of a camp that had corrupted itself; every one which sought the LORD went out unto the tabernacle without the camp. When Moses went out unto the tabernacle, all the people rose up and stood every man at his tent door and looked after Moses until he was gone in; and the cloudy pillar descended and stood at the door of the tabernacle, and the LORD talked with Moses, and all the people rose up and worshipped, every man in his tent door. The LORD spake unto Moses face to face, as a man speaketh unto his friend. That is not Moses looking eye to eye at the Lord; it means there was no mediator between Moses and the Lord, for Moses himself was the mediator between the Lord and the people, and the Lord spoke to him directly. His servant Joshua, the son of Nun, a young man, departed not out of the tabernacle. Joshua was a true disciple, a learner, eager to stay by Moses' side and learn; the Lord knew his spirit.

Moses pled with the Lord: thou hast said, I know thee by name, and thou hast also found grace in my sight; now therefore shew me now thy way, that I may know thee, that I may find grace in thy sight; and consider that this nation is thy people. The Lord answered, My presence shall go with thee, and I will give thee rest. And Moses said, If thy presence go not with me, carry us not up hence; for wherein shall it be known here that I and thy people have found grace in thy sight? is it not in that thou goest with us? so shall we be separated, I and thy people, from all the people that are upon the face of the earth. The presence of the Most High in the midst is how Israel is known to be separated from all the nations, and it ties back to the sabbath sign: when Israel keeps the sabbath and gathers in his name, the Lord and Christ are in the midst.

Moses said, I beseech thee, shew me thy glory. And he said, I will make all my goodness pass before thee, and I will proclaim the name of the LORD before thee, and will be gracious to whom I will be gracious, and will shew mercy on whom I will shew mercy, then and in the future as well. Thou canst not see my face: for there shall no man see me, and live. In verse 11 Christ spoke to Moses on the Lord's behalf, with Moses as the mediator to the people; here it is the Father of heaven and earth himself, and no man can see his face and live. Behold, there is a place by me, and thou shalt stand upon a rock: I will put thee in a clift of the rock, and will cover thee with my hand while I pass by; and I will take away mine hand, and thou shalt see my back parts, but my face shall not be seen. Moses beheld the similitude of the LORD, the back parts of his glory, never his face.

When the people saw that Moses delayed to come down out of the mount, they gathered unto Aaron: Up, make us gods, which shall go before us; for as for this Moses, we wot not what is become of him. Any time deliverance did not come when Israel wanted it, the nation rebelled, and Moses and the leadership got the blame; the same spirit is against the leadership of Israel to this day. Aaron said break off the golden earrings which are in the ears of your wives, of your sons, and of your daughters. Men and women both wore earrings in the scriptures, and it is not sin. Aaron received the gold, fashioned it with a graving tool, and made a molten calf, and they said, These be thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt. Aaron saw the miracles in Egypt and was set up as high priest, yet he succumbed to the pressure of the people; that is why the Lord chose Moses specifically to lead, because Moses could not be moved by any means. Aaron built an altar before it and made proclamation, To morrow is a feast to the LORD; and the people rose up early, offered burnt offerings and peace offerings, sat down to eat and to drink, and rose up to play. Israel kept provoking God, and the Lord still brought the nation into the promised land as he promised Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

The Lord told Moses, Go, get thee down; for thy people, which thou broughtest out of the land of Egypt, have corrupted themselves. They turned aside quickly out of the way, made a molten calf, worshipped it, and sacrificed thereunto. Not forty days gone, and they had already left his commandments. The spirit that was in Israel in Egypt was still in Israel when they left. It is the same coming into this truth: the evil carried in from the world will corrupt you and turn you from the Lord if it is not put off. I have seen this people, and, behold, it is a stiffnecked people. That has been Israel's reputation with the Father from the beginning; without the laws of God we are a carnal, rebellious people, which is why these last days call for humbleness and repentance, not bringing the world's rhetoric into the congregation. Now therefore let me alone, that my wrath may wax hot against them, and that I may consume them: and I will make of thee a great nation. Moses was of the tribe of Levi, of the seed of Jacob, so the Lord could have started over with him.

Moses besought the LORD his God: LORD, why doth thy wrath wax hot against thy people, which thou hast brought forth out of the land of Egypt with great power, and with a mighty hand? Moses had compassion and stood in the middle, interceding and mediating between the people and God. Wherefore should the Egyptians speak, and say, For mischief did he bring them out, to slay them in the mountains? And remember Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, to whom thou swarest by thine own self to multiply their seed as the stars of heaven, and to give the land to their seed for ever. And the LORD repented of the evil which he thought to do unto his people. The Most High does not repent as a man; he has no one to answer to, he simply turned from the anger of that moment. He was never going to break his covenant, for consuming the people would have destroyed all the seed of Jacob except Moses; Moses was there to remind him of his own word. From the questions: the Lord dealt with Moses on a level where Moses could speak to him so, but the outcome stood on what was declared from the beginning; had it been his pleasure to destroy, nothing Moses said could have stayed it.

Moses went down from the mount with the two tables of the testimony in his hand, written on both their sides; the tables were the work of God, and the writing was the writing of God, graven upon the tables. Joshua heard the noise of the people and said, There is a noise of war in the camp; Moses answered, It is not the voice of them that shout for mastery, neither the voice of them that cry for being overcome, but the noise of them that sing do I hear. They were feasting and dancing around the idol. Joshua's loyalty at the mount is one of the main reasons the Lord chose him to succeed Moses. As soon as he came nigh unto the camp and saw the calf and the dancing, Moses' anger waxed hot, and he cast the tables out of his hands and brake them beneath the mount. He took the calf which they had made, burnt it in the fire, ground it to powder, strawed it upon the water, and made the children of Israel drink of it. Our forefathers were no joke about the law; Nehemiah likewise put hands on those who profaned the sabbath in his day.

Moses said unto Aaron, What did this people unto thee, that thou hast brought so great a sin upon them? He had left Aaron in charge, and came back to a camp deep in wickedness. Aaron answered, Let not the anger of my lord wax hot: thou knowest the people, that they are set on mischief; they said make us gods, I cast the gold into the fire, and there came out this calf. A leader cannot blame the congregation, the same excuse Saul gave; the charge has to be carried. The psalm gives the depth of it: they soon forgat his works and waited not for his counsel, they made a calf in Horeb and changed their glory into the similitude of an ox that eateth grass, and they forgat God their saviour, which had done great things in Egypt, wondrous works in the land of Ham, and terrible things by the Red sea.

The people were naked, for Aaron had made them naked unto their shame among their enemies. That is the same nakedness of [Genesis 3](/bible/genesis/3), the shame of sin uncovered. Moses stood in the gate of the camp and said, Who is on the LORD's side? let him come unto me. And all the sons of Levi gathered themselves together unto him. Every man put his sword by his side and went in and out from gate to gate throughout the camp, and there fell of the people that day about three thousand men. The Lord chose those particular ones to die; that spirit would have wrecked the nation down the road, so he moved it out of the congregation. Do not be broken when someone leaves the truth; the Lord moves spiritually. Consecrate yourselves to day to the LORD, even every man upon his son, and upon his brother, that he may bestow upon you a blessing this day.

Moses said unto the people, Ye have sinned a great sin. They had broken the first two commandments just given at Sinai: no other gods before him, and no graven image to bow down to and serve. Moses returned unto the LORD to mediate: yet now, if thou wilt forgive their sin; and if not, blot me, I pray thee, out of thy book which thou hast written. That is a real leader, putting himself in the way of harm for his people. The Lord answered, Whosoever hath sinned against me, him will I blot out of my book; therefore now go, lead the people, and mine Angel shall go before thee; nevertheless in the day when I visit I will visit their sin upon them. And the LORD plagued the people, because they made the calf, which Aaron made.

Chapter 39 is the application of the instructions of chapter 28: the holy garments for Aaron the priest, the clothes of service to do service in the holy place, made of the blue, purple, and scarlet as the Lord commanded Moses.

The breastplate carried four rows of stones, and the stones were according to the names of the children of Israel, twelve according to their names, like the engravings of a signet, every one with his name according to the twelve tribes; the shoulders of the ephod carried onyx stones graven the same way, stones for a memorial to the children of Israel. The Most High had us representing: when the priest stepped on the scene you already knew what nationality he was. Nationality is very important to the Lord, and he took it very seriously.

The pomegranates and the bells of gold went upon the hem of the robe round about; the word keeps saying round about, because the fringes go all throughout the garment, round about, not gathered only at four corners. Old depictions show Israelites with the fringes all the way around, and it would not hurt to put them all throughout, out of the fear of God.

They made the plate of the holy crown of pure gold, written like the engravings of a signet, HOLINESS TO THE LORD, fastened on high upon the mitre with a lace of blue. Black man, this is your heritage: our forefathers the priests wore crowns of real pure gold. It is a blessing to come back to this knowledge; they will not teach you this anywhere else.

Thus was all the work of the tabernacle finished, and the children of Israel did according to all that the Lord commanded Moses; they brought every piece to Moses, and he looked upon all the work, and behold, they had done it as the Lord had commanded, and Moses blessed them. It is like getting a building today and doing all the painting, sanding, nailing, and screwing, and then standing back and seeing the finished product: all praises to the Most High, we did it; then the people are blessed.

Moses went up from the plains of Moab unto the mountain of Nebo, to the top of Pisgah, over against Jericho, and the Most High shewed him all the land: Gilead unto Dan, Naphtali, Ephraim and Manasseh, Judah unto the utmost sea, the south, and the plain of the valley of Jericho unto Zoar. This is the land which I sware unto Abraham, unto Isaac, and unto Jacob, saying, I will give it unto thy seed: I have caused thee to see it with thine eyes, but thou shalt not go over thither. Moses could see it, but he could not go into it.

So Moses the servant of the Lord died there in the land of Moab, according to the word of the Lord, and he was buried in a valley in the land of Moab, over against Bethpeor: but no man knoweth of his sepulchre unto this day. So do not go trying to find it. Moses was an hundred and twenty years old when he died: his eye was not dim, nor his natural force abated. He was not weak, old, and sickly like a man about to drop dead; he was in full strength, and still he had to go up and die because he could not enter the land.

The children of Israel wept for Moses in the plains of Moab thirty days, until the days of weeping and mourning for Moses were ended. Joshua the son of Nun was full of the spirit of wisdom; for Moses had laid his hands upon him. Joshua was Moses' protege, and he carried the spirit Moses had, a great leader compassionate for the people; and the children of Israel hearkened unto him, and did as the Lord commanded Moses.

And there arose not a prophet since in Israel like unto Moses, whom the Lord knew face to face. This verse is heavy because of a doctrine: some say Joshua was the prophet of [Deuteronomy 18:18](/bible/deuteronomy/18#v18), the prophet raised up like unto Moses, and therefore there is no Christ. But the scripture that acknowledges Joshua rising up with the spirit upon him says in the same breath that there arose not a prophet since in Israel like unto Moses. Joshua was a mighty prophet, but he did not fit that word; Christ did. None matched all the signs and the wonders which the Lord sent Moses to do in the land of Egypt, and all that mighty hand, and all the great terror which Moses shewed in the sight of all Israel. With this the Torah, the books of Moses, is finished.
